title: Kenyan Mango Coconut Dessert
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Mango Coconut Dessert — ripe mango slices bathed in a fragrant coconut cream sauce with cardamom, lime, and honey. Two of Kenya's greatest ingredients together in the simplest, most beautiful tropical dessert.
longDesc: Mango and coconut are the two most iconic flavours of the Kenyan coast, and this dessert brings them together in the simplest, most direct way. Ripe mango slices are dressed in a lightly spiced coconut cream with cardamom, lime zest, and honey — the combination is refreshing, fragrant, and sophisticated without requiring any cooking skill beyond slicing fruit. It is the Swahili coastal answer to the question of what to serve after a rich fish curry.
ingredients: 3 large ripe mangoes — peeled and sliced
2 tbsp desiccated coconut — toasted, for garnish
steps: Peel and slice the mangoes elegantly.
Arrange on a serving plate or in individual bowls.
Combine coconut cream, honey, cardamom, lime zest, and lime juice. Whisk until smooth.
Pour the coconut cream sauce over and around the mango slices.
Scatter toasted coconut and fresh mint over the top.
Serve immediately or refrigerate for up to 1 hour.
chefTips: The ripest, most fragrant mango makes this extraordinary — settle for nothing less.
Coconut cream (not coconut milk) gives a richer, more luxurious sauce.
Toast the desiccated coconut in a dry pan until golden for maximum flavour.
commonMistakes: Using coconut milk instead of coconut cream — too thin.
Under-ripe mango — the dessert loses its character entirely.

faqs.a: Yes — prepare the coconut cream sauce and slice the mangoes separately. Combine up to 30 minutes before serving. Do not prepare more than 1 hour ahead as the mango softens.

cookingScience: Ripe mango contains over 300 volatile aromatic compounds that give it its distinctive fragrance. Cardamom's main aroma compound (1,8-cineole) and the terpenes in the mango's aroma complement each other — both belong to the terpene family, creating a harmonious, layered fragrance.
sustainabilityTips: Kenyan mangoes from local farms in season are the most sustainable choice.
storage: Best eaten fresh. Refrigerate without dressing for up to 4 hours.
healthBenefits: Mango is exceptionally rich in vitamins C and A.
culturalNote: Mango coconut dessert embodies the Swahili coastal philosophy of combining the region's two greatest natural gifts — the exceptional mangoes of the Kenyan coast and the ubiquitous coconut — into something effortlessly beautiful.
